notes:
### Player
- **1 deck** fits all controls in one row, leaving more room for the
  library.
- Flatter player buttons with smaller corners and a little depth.
- **Smoother waveforms:** they now move at your screen's full rate (up to
  120 fps on ProMotion MacBooks, before 60). Settings → Player & mixer can
  cap the frame rate at 60 fps, with a separate cap on battery (60 fps by
  default), and show the frame rate on the waveform.
- Switching from 2 decks to 1 while deck B plays asks first, then stops
  deck B (it used to keep playing out of sight).
- **Loops:** IN / OUT, RELOOP / EXIT, auto loops from 1/4 to 32 beats with
  halve and double, all on the beat with quantize, seamless with Master
  Tempo.
- **CUES list:** every cue and saved loop of the track. Go to one, name it,
  change its colour or delete it, and save the deck's loop with the track.
- Saved loops are saved to Engine DJ and Rekordbox in Sync → Cue & grid
  edits, like cues.
- **Beatgrids edited in Krate can now be saved to Rekordbox** too (into
  its analysis files, exactly as Rekordbox saves a grid edit, backed up
  first).

### Other
- **Album art loads right away:** Krate keeps small copies of the covers
  instead of reading every audio file again at each start (the decks'
  covers too). Settings → Appearance → Album art shows the cache and can
  clear it, all of it or for chosen playlists.
- Tidy says so when the Rekordbox library uses Cloud Library Sync (changes
  then go to your other computers too).
- The battery is shown in the top right corner on laptops: charge, a bolt
  while charging or a plug on the adapter, and the time left on battery or
  until full.
- Updates come out for each system as soon as it's built, so Macs no
  longer wait for the Windows build. If you check for updates in between,
  Krate says the download for your computer isn't ready yet.

### Fixes
- The track list's column headings scroll sideways with the list, so they
  stay above their columns.
- Loading a new track into the master deck no longer changes the tempo of
  the synced deck: the master passes to the other deck first, as on CDJs.
